chunks: Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad narrated to us, from Aḥmad ibn al-Ḥasan ibn Abān, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Jabalah, from ʿAlāʾ, from Muḥammad ibn Muslim, from one of the two — meaning Abū Jaʿfar and Abū ʿAbd Allāh, peace be upon them.

He said: The month of Ramadan is affected by deficiency just as the other months are affected. So when you have fasted twenty-nine days and then the sky becomes cloudy, then complete the count as thirty.
2- ʿAlī ibn Mahziyār, from ʿAmr ibn ʿUthmān, from al-Mufaḍḍal, from Zayd al-Shaḥḥām, from Abū ʿAbd Allāh, peace be upon him.

He was asked about the crescents. He said: They are the crescents of the months. So when you see the crescent, then fast; and when you see it, then break the fast. I said: What if the month was twenty-nine days — should I make up that day? He said: No, unless upright witnesses testify for you. If they testify that they had seen the crescent before that, then make up that day.
3- From him, from al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī, from al-Qāsim ibn ʿUrwah, from Abū al-ʿAbbās, from Abū ʿAbd Allāh, peace be upon him.
He said: Fasting is based on sighting, and breaking the fast is based on sighting; and sighting is not that one person sees it, nor two, nor fifty.
4- From him, from ʿUthmān ibn ʿĪsā, from Rifāʿah, from Abū ʿAbd Allāh, peace be upon him.

He said: The fasting of the month of Ramadan is by sighting, not by conjecture. The month of Ramadan may be twenty-nine days, and it may be thirty; it is subject to what affects the months in terms of completion and deficiency.
5- From him, from Muḥammad ibn Abī ʿUmayr, from Ayyūb and Ḥammād, from Muḥammad ibn Muslim, from Abū Jaʿfar, peace be upon him.

He said: When you see the crescent, then fast; and when you see it, then break the fast. It is not by opinion nor by supposition, but rather by sighting. He said: And sighting is not that ten stand looking, then one says, 'There it is,' while nine look and do not see it. When one sees it, ten and a thousand see it. And when there is an impediment, then complete Shaʿbān as thirty.
6- al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd, from Muḥammad ibn Fuḍayl, from Abū al-Ṣabbāḥ and Ṣafwān, from Ibn Muskān, from al-Ḥalabī, all together from Abū ʿAbd Allāh, peace be upon him.

He was asked about the crescents, so he said: They are the crescents of the months. So when you see the crescent, then fast; and when you see it, then break the fast. I said: What if the month was twenty-nine days — should I make up that day? He said: No, unless upright witnesses testify for you. If they testify that they had seen the crescent before that, then make up that day.
7- From him, from Ṣafwān, from Manṣūr ibn Ḥāzim, from Abū ʿAbd Allāh, peace be upon him.
He said: Fast upon sighting the crescent, and break the fast upon sighting it. If two approved witnesses testify before you that they saw it, then make it up.
8- From him, from al-Qāsim, from Abān, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Abī ʿAbd Allāh.

He said: I asked Abū ʿAbd Allāh, peace be upon him, about the crescent of Ramadan when it is obscured from us on the twenty-ninth of Shaʿbān. He said: Do not fast unless you see it. If the people of another town testify, then make it up.
9- From him, from Yūnus ibn ʿAqīl, from Muḥammad ibn Qays, from Abū Jaʿfar, peace be upon him.

He said: Amīr al-Muʾminīn, peace be upon him, said: When you see the crescent, then break the fast, or let upright evidence from the Muslims testify to it. If you do not see the crescent except from the middle of the day or its end, then complete the fast until night. And if it is obscured from you, then count thirty and then break the fast.
10- From him, from Faḍālah, from Sayf ibn ʿAmīrah, from Isḥāq ibn ʿAmmār, from Abū ʿAbd Allāh, peace be upon him.

He said: In the Book of ʿAlī, peace be upon him: Fast upon its sighting, and break the fast upon its sighting; beware of doubt and conjecture. If it is hidden from you, then complete the first month as thirty.
11- From him, from Faḍālah, from Sayf, from al-Fuḍayl ibn ʿUthmān, from Abū ʿAbd Allāh, peace be upon him.
He said: Nothing is binding upon the people of the qiblah except sighting, and nothing is binding upon the Muslims except sighting.

key_terms.الرُّؤْيَةُ: actual sighting of the crescent as the basis for legal determination
key_terms.الشَّكَّ: doubt, which must be avoided in determining the fast
key_terms.الظَّنِّ: conjecture, which is rejected as a basis here
key_terms.النُّقْصَانِ: deficiency, meaning a month being twenty-nine days
key_terms.الْهِلَالَ: the new crescent moon marking the lunar month
key_terms.بَيِّنَةٌ عُدُولٌ: upright legal testimony from reliable witnesses
key_terms.ثَلَاثِينَ: thirty, the number completed when visibility is obstructed
key_terms.شَهْرُ رَمَضَانَ: the month of Ramadan, whose beginning and end are under discussion

ai.seo_question: How is the crescent of Ramadan and Shawwal established according to these hadith?
ai.summary: These narrations state that the beginning and end of Ramadan are established by sighting the crescent, not by conjecture, opinion, or doubt. They also affirm that Ramadan, like other lunar months, may be either twenty-nine or thirty days, and that when the sky is obscured one completes the preceding month as thirty unless reliable testimony establishes the crescent.
